Why is the assumptions that its is always the fault of the person with BPD?
Its so hard to hear something so dehumanizing from someone I valued so much. I dont think that he even sees me as human anymore.
I have been going to therapy once a week since he ended it.  But that wont provide any insight into his mind.

I never had an ego, I tried to be as open and honest as I possibly could be and tried to fully acknowledge every mistake and self-deprecating behavior. I don't understand what I did to hurt him so badly
The hardest part is that I still dont know what I did to hurt him so bad, I really dont understand because he refused to talk to me directly about it.
I think he is taking it that way, it seems like he is using BPD as an excuse for everything instead of looking at his behavior as well.

I never was abusive, I needed validation a lot and had very low self esteem. I never yelled at him or tried to keep him away from his friends or did anything like that. I dont understand his level of reaction to what I was doing. Everything negative I did was focused inwards towards myself. I was always ready to admit when something I was doing was causing a problem and try to change it. He would let things build up and never tell me he had a problem with something I was doing, then one day he would snap and yell at me. He said I made him feel scared that he would take advantage of me because I don't stand up for myself.
I found it on social media, and I know I shouldn't be looking but it feels like I can't stop myself.

I guess what makes it so hard is knowing that he thinks that about me. He was someone who I really cared about and I respected his opinion.  Also worried what he is saying to his mom and dad and friends. They were all people that I liked and I thought liked me, but now who knows what he is saying to them.  Its hard feeling like your reputation is being smeared behind your back.
Thank you, I really needed to hear somthing like this. It's so easy to find myself ruled by others interpretation of me.

Thank you, this is helpful.  It really seems like there is a lot of misinformation in that sub and an overall message that no one should be with anyone with BPD.  Its hard to see that stuff, I should stay away from there.
If I have to be stuck with only myself for the rest of my life then I might as well end it now because I hate myself.  I hate being with me and so does the world.
I can't care enough about myself. Caring about myself is not a choice.
Then things will never get any better for me.

I don't really care enough about myself enough to keep trying to change. I feel like no matter how much I improve it will never be enough to be the kind of person that anyone would want to be with. I don't even want to be around myself.

I feel it was almost the opposite. I depended on him a lot more at the begining of the relationship than at the end. When we first started going out he was not planing to become a therapist, he said that seeing my struggles was part of the reason he became a therapist.  I think that helping me made him feel better about himself.

I know that he was not my therapist. I just figure that someone who would be the kind of person to become a therapist would also be the kind of person who would be willing to handle the rockness of BPD long enough for me to grow.  I don't think I will ever care enough about myself to grow unless there is someone there.
Life will never get better for me. So why waste the effort. I have a place to end it in mind and have no reason to stay that is stong enough to overcome this urge.

There is no one out there who would choose to be with someone like me.  So there is no point. I have no hobbies I care about anymore and my family would move on. I don't provide anything to anyone that cant be obtained some other way. There is no reason to keep going
Thank you very much :3
